subject: CloudScale DPA: telemetry & ops subprocessor carveout - product/security review
messages:
From: Sasha Kim <sasha.kim@cloudscale.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudScale DPA redline - telemetry subprocessor carveout

Hi Sean —

Attached is CloudScale's redline of the DPA. Two items we need explicit confirmation on before legal will proceed: 1) TelemetryOps Inc. (our ops vendor) is listed as an allowed subprocessor for runtime telemetry; we need clarity on exact telemetry fields, retention, and whether Redwood or CloudScale controls KMS keys for any exported logs. 2) For runtime traces we need an option to have logs delivered to our customer-managed S3 or a signed-forwarding arrangement; CloudScale will not accept unbounded vendor-side retention without contract.

Can you confirm product/security are aligned on the permitted signal set and a path for a short-term exception if needed? Procurement has asked for a go/no-go by EOD Wednesday so we can meet our internal review cycle.

Attachments: CloudScale_DPA_redline_20280610.pdf (pdf, 1 page summary + redline)

Thanks,
Sasha
Legal — CloudScale

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: CloudScale DPA redline - telemetry subprocessor carveout

Looping product/security — CloudScale (large pilot) has redlined the DPA to require explicit subprocessor allowance for TelemetryOps Inc. and wants either customer-managed delivery of runtime traces or strict retention limits. Procurement needs an answer by EOD Wed.

High-level ask for product/security:
- Define the minimal telemetry signal set we can commit to (no request/response bodies, no raw prompts, no user PII).
- Can we support a customer-managed delivery option (S3 sink) for this account?
- If not, propose retention window (they asked for short retention). Security: confirm what controls we can offer on KMS and whether TelemetryOps can be scopped to metric/ops-only (no session contents).

Proposed quick mitigations to consider: prefix-only traces, hash identifiers, 14-30 day rolling retention for runtime traces, sampling at 0.1-1% for debug traces, and a short-term contractual exception tied to an audit schedule.

Please respond with a recommended path + who needs to approve (product lead / security manager). I can escalate to legal/exec if we need a faster SLA.

Thanks — Sean
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudScale DPA redline - telemetry subprocessor carveout

Thanks for the heads-up, Sean. Security concerns / required items before we can sign off on an exception: 

1) Subprocessor proof: TelemetryOps must provide SOC 2 Type II report and our third-party security questionnaire responses. No onboarding without evidence.
2) KMS / key control: We do not share Redwood customer encryption keys with subprocessors. If CloudScale requires customer-managed keys, propose log delivery to their S3 or an Azure/GCP customer sink.
3) Data minimization: Product must commit to a bounded signal set (no prompts, no outputs, no raw user content). Hash any identifiers and remove high-risk metadata.
4) Retention: Security-preferred retention for vendor-side telemetry is 14 days for traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics. If CloudScale insists on different timing, Legal must capture an explicit exception and audit cadence.
5) Access control & audit: TelemetryOps accounts must be scopped to read-only aggregated metrics (no session replay). All access must be logged and surfaced to CloudScale on request.

I attached our telemetry security checklist — fill sections A2 (subproc evidence) and B4 (delivery options) and return. If product proposes a tech mitigation we can consider a time-limited exception (30 days) pending a successful third-party assessment.

Attachments: sec_checklist_telemetry.md

Olga
Security Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudScale DPA redline - telemetry subprocessor carveout

Appreciate the quick flag. Product's proposed mitigations below — these are realistic to implement within a short engineering sprint for a pilot account, but we'd want a formal exception window while the security assessment completes.

Proposed scope & technical controls:
- Signal set: metrics + anonymized runtime telemetry (latency, model id, step durations, basic invocation metadata). Explicit NO: request/response bodies, raw prompts, user-provided files.
- Identifier handling: deterministic hashing of session_id and user_id before any export; salt stored per-customer and rotated quarterly.
- Traces: prefix-only stack/ops traces; no token-level content.
- Retention: 14-day rolling retention for runtime traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics. Can shorten to 7/30 if legal demands.
- Delivery: offer customer-managed sink (S3) as default for CloudScale. If they prefer vendor-side ingestion, require TelemetryOps to sign a subproc addendum and provide SOC2 evidence.
- Operational: sampling configurable per-customer (default 0.5%), and an opt-out telemetry toggle in the Console for enterprise customers.

I'll drop a short spec doc this morning (attached: proposed_mop_v1.docx) and can scope the minimal sprint for enabling sinks + hashing. If security confirms SOC2 and approves the 14-day window, I recommend Legal accept a 30-day business-exception window while third-party evidence is gathered.

Ben
Group Product Manager — Runtime

From: CloudScale Legal <legal@cloudscale.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Kim <sasha.kim@cloudscale.com>, Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudScale DPA redline - telemetry subprocessor carveout

Sean / team —

Thanks for the quick internal coordination. The proposal to offer a customer-managed S3 sink is acceptable to CloudScale legal as a preferred path; we'll take that as the default route while TelemetryOps completes SOC2. Procurement asks for a simple timeline: can Redwood enable the S3 sink + hashing for our account within 2 weeks? If yes, we'll proceed with the DPA redline including a 30-day conditional exception tied to SOC2 evidence.

Please also confirm whether any of the proposed telemetry will include IP addresses or user-agent strings (CloudScale requires those fields be excluded or pseudonymized).

If you can provide a short implementation timeline and confirm the fields list, we will circulate the revised DPA to our stakeholders.

Best,
CloudScale Legal
